title: The Signature Vision: Robot Volcano Probes
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Robot Volcano Probes.

Signature probe hulls program, charter one: master heat-shield bots at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale probe logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate lava sampling systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Robot Volcano Probes becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

description:
First probe hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and telemetry construction sites.

What must be true first: the heat-shield bots results have to replicate outside the lab, probe logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and lava sampling operations need a year of continuous runtime. Signals to watch: peer-reviewed heat-shield bots demonstrations, probe logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting lava sampling uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Robot Volcano Probes
definition: Estimates Robot Volcano Probes readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Robot Volcano Probes components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a probe hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Robot Volcano Probes Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Robot Volcano Probes operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Robot Volcano Probes installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 71682 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where heat-shield bots monitoring, probe logistics redundancy, or lava sampling maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Robot Volcano Probes Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Robot Volcano Probes: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Robot Volcano Probes — robots sampling active volcanoes.

Phase 1 — Prove (heat-shield bots): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (probe logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (lava sampling): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (telemetry): probe hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and geology-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
